newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli stocks end higher on fall in the shekel.
newsitem.headline: Israeli stocks end higher on fall in the shekel.

text.p: Tel Aviv shares closed higher on Thursday in active trading in response to a sharp decline in the shekel against the dollar, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.84 percent, or 1.65 points, to 197.97 on all-share turnover of 77 million shekels against 62 million on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 0.72 percent to 207.52.

"Activity is rising and investors are more optimistic now," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank. "The main reason for today's rise was the decline of the shekel, which it's thought will boost Israeli exports."

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2560 shekels against 3.2320 on Thursday after newspaper reports, later denied, said the Bank of Israel would make a sharp reduction in short-term interest rates if the government cut the 1997 budget by seven billion shekels as planned.

"Investors are still waiting to see what will happen with the approval of the 1997 budget," said Michael Weiss of Evergreen Capital Markets. "The (initial) reaction to Netanyahu's announcement was very moderate. Investors are still waiting for a final approval (by parliament)."

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday that the Treasury would propose an additional two billion shekels in budget cuts for next year by early December. The reductions will come on top of 4.9 billion shekels in cuts the government has already submitted to parliament.
Although two companies, Discount Investment Corp. and Clal Electronic Industries reported big drops in third-quarter net profit on Thursday that was due to their holdings in Scitex Corp.
"Most of the earnings reports that have been published have been positive so far, and the mood in the market is very positive," the Mizrahi trader said.

Clal Electronics surged 4.25 percent to 25,610 despite a quarterly net loss of 49.5 million shekels against a net profit of 8.1 million shekels in the same period last year. Traders said Clal's results were within expectations and that investors now expect it would show improved results in the future.
Discount Investments, however, fell 1.0 percent to 19,905 after reporting a third-quarter net profit of 5.01 million shekels against 44.14 million shekels a year earlier.
Tadiran fell 3.5 percent to 1,406, which traders said closed the difference with the company's New York share price.

The most active shares were Bank Hapoalim, which rose 2.5 percent to 476 on volume of 4.1 million shekels; Bank Leumi, which gained 0.5 percent to 395 on turnover of 3.1 million shekels; and Dead Sea Works, which closed unchanged at 807 on volume of 2.4 million shekels.
